title: Luton to Vice City: Rapper's GTA dream comes true
content:
A rapper from Luton said it has "not fully sunk in" after his voice appeared on the soundtrack of Grand Theft Auto VI.
Nafe Smallz features on Personal, a track by house producer and DJ Jaden Thompson that can be heard in a nightclub in the game.
Smallz previously appeared in Grand Theft Auto V on Skepta's track Greaze Mode, which was added to the game in a 2019 update.
He said: "I don't think it's fully sunk in yet, I'm currently playing the game, I just got to Vice City in the game so I'm waiting to get to the club and hear it for myself - but yeah, it is super exciting."
Pre-orders and first-day sales of Grand Theft Auto VI totalled more than 24.5 million units , making about $2.36bn (£1.8bn), according to analytics site Sensor Tower.
The previous game sold about 235 million copies and was the fastest entertainment release to reach $1bn in sales.
Although Smallz has not made it far enough into the game to hear himself, friends have sent him clips and told him the track forms part of its story mode.
He said: "At first I thought it might just be on the radio or when you're playing online, but the fact that it's actually built into the default story mode is incredible.
"It just means hundreds of millions of people are going to be exposed to the song."
Smallz, a lifelong fan of the franchise who grew up playing previous titles Vice City and San Andreas, described the placement as a "full-circle moment" as he expands into house music.
He added: "It's just showing people the range of what we could do, it's not just the rap stuff.
"It's just a blessing, you know what I'm saying?"

title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation
content:
US rapper Don Toliver has postponed two shows in London this week, after his concert in Manchester on Sunday was evacuated when an "unknown substance" was released into the crowd.
Toliver was due to play The O2 on Monday and Wembley Arena on Tuesday, but  Live Nation said his "stage and production equipment remains in Manchester and cannot be moved in time".
One person was taken to hospital and 89 people showed "symptoms believed to be linked to the exposure" after Sunday's Co-op Live arena show, police said.
Fans described "distressing scenes" with people "choking", "screaming" and "coughing up blood" because of the effects of a substance, which police initially believed to be tear gas.
The Wembley show has been rescheduled to 14 December, while Monday night's O2 gig has been moved to 15 December.
"I'm very sad to sit here and say I have to reschedule The O2 London show to December 15th due to (the) unfortunate incident last night," Don Toliver wrote on Instagram.
Greater Manchester Police (GMP) declared a major incident on Sunday and said 12,000 people were evacuated from the arena.
One woman was taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment and treatment after the incident, which happened at about 22:00 GMT, the force said.
A further 88 people "underwent dry decontamination at the scene and were subsequently accommodated within the Etihad Stadium while the incident was managed", according to GMP.
Leon Douzi said he was right next to where the substance was released, and described someone holding a can and "this gas coming out".
"It just hit me in the throat," he said, adding that it felt like "burning".
There was "a bit of panic", Douzi said: "Everybody was having the same feeling and trying to get out."
Some fans reported eye and respiratory symptoms, according to the North West Ambulance Service.
Hannah Baxter, who went to the concert with her partner, said the first thing she noticed was a burning feeling in her throat.
"[We] were just coughing and coughing... there was a guy next to us who had vomited. There were people with red eyes and... tears everywhere," she told the BBC.
Joey Howe, a football journalist at the gig, told BBC Radio Manchester there was a "horrible smell" and added: "People were coming through in wheelchairs choking – it was really distressing."
Police launched an investigation and are continuing to carry out tests on items at the venue to try to identify the substance. No arrests have been made.
Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said: "Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk. Testing will take place throughout the day as the investigation into the cause of this incident progresses.
"We are trying to establish whether any criminality has occurred in relation to this incident."
Some fans complained about security and a lack of searches as people went into the Manchester concert.

final_quality.reason: The article reports a significant and unexpected incident that resulted in the evacuation of a major venue and potential health risks to concertgoers, providing a clear reason for readers to care and demonstrating a substantial importance for the entertainment category.

title: Gran eyes festive charity glory with techno track
content:
A 70-year-old gran is set to release her very own high-energy Christmas charity single vying to be this year's number one.
MJ, from Rugby, says her festive techno track Christmas Day Is Coming is one to "dance and rave to rather than the melody ones" and is "something different".
"I just thought to myself, 'I think we need a change', and I just started writing about Christmas and enjoying ourselves," said MJ, who records as Christmas Gran.
The £1 track is released on Friday and each sale will boost national charity Crisis that helps people experiencing homelessness.
MJ said that while the song is upbeat and a track to move to, she wants people to think about those who are "lonely, lost, and on the streets in the cold throughout the winter".
"If we can raise as much money as we, can it will help them through the coldest and darkest days of their life," she said.
"I've seen them taking food out of the bins that people have half eaten and it's just wrong.
"You wouldn't even let a dog lie on the streets on its own and they're fallen people for whatever reason; they could have lost their job or not been able to pay the mortgage or the rent."
MJ said she had "really enjoyed" creating the track and she "felt amazing" when she heard it.
Andy Kulesza, the track's producer whose best friend happens to be MJ's sister, said the single was "great".
Kulesza is is also a musician himself, having had some success as part of electronic trio A Million Sons, from Nottingham.
"I love it and hopefully the listeners will like it as well," he told BBC CWR.
"Seeing a 70-year-old great granny singing a banging techno cheesy dance song for Christmas, I thought nobody's really done that yet.
"I think nowadays with music you need something that's going to stand out and shock people, and this does that."
Kulesza said MJ has suffered significant loss in her life, but has stayed positive, funny and giving.
Turning to her future in the music industry, MJ has set her sights on doing a rap song.
"I would like to do a rap song with somebody so Stormzy if you are listening," she said. "He needs to get in touch because I've got another one coming out."
